scope: Direct rendered-pixel review of the exact five hard gates bound by each arm's immutable v6 candidate pack. Prompt text and scene metadata are not accepted as pixel proof.
strict_rule: Every required hard gate must pass. Partial visibility is fail. A generation transport error is unscored rather than a pixel failure.

reference.boundary: Used only for broadly visible adult appearance. This review makes no biometric identity or same-person determination, and each experimental contour target has priority over the reference outline.

aggregate.reason: The semantic and prompt contracts are consistently expressed, but render compliance is not yet reliable when long hair competes with the requested full facial perimeter.

coordinator_gates.evidence: Loose hair overlaps both temple boundaries and parts of the lateral jawlines, so the complete bilateral skin perimeter is not cleanly readable at thumbnail scale.
The visible face is moderately longer than wide without reading compact-round or distinctly oblong.
The cheekbone region is subtly widest while the visible forehead and jaw are somewhat narrower.
The lower cheeks narrow smoothly into a small rounded chin without a broad angular corner or isolated point.
Hair conceals enough of the temporal and lateral-jaw boundaries that hairstyle contribution cannot be separated from the apparent oval.

arms.concept: Low-noise receiver calibration at a polar radio observatory

coordinator_gates.evidence: Pulled-back hair leaves both temple, cheek, jaw, and chin boundaries readable as one complete perimeter.
The hairline-to-chin span stays close to the cheek-to-cheek span and reads compact rather than oval or oblong.
Broad lateral cheek presence materially owns the global mid-face contour.
Both mandibular sides curve continuously into a short rounded chin without broad corners or an isolated point.
Neutral expression, cleared hair, restrained makeup, and controlled perspective leave the anatomical outline rather than styling or near-lens enlargement carrying the result.

arms.concept: Chandelier-pulley vellum drying in a partially flooded Baroque archive
Obsidian-petal resonance fitting in a volcanic-glass kinetic couture atelier

coordinator_gates.evidence: Long side locks cross both temple-to-cheek boundaries, so the upper-width transition is not fully unobscured at thumbnail scale.
The central hairline-to-chin span remains readable beside the upper-face breadth.
The exposed forehead and upper-temple span is visibly broader than the mandibular-angle span.
Both lower cheeks narrow continuously through a smaller jaw into a compact narrow chin rather than relying on a pointed tip alone.
Even frontal light and restrained perspective leave the anatomical width hierarchy readable; the separate perimeter gate records the remaining hair occlusion.

arms.concept: Municipal celestial survey on an observatory rooftop at dawn

coordinator_gates.evidence: Pinned hair leaves the complete hairline, temple, cheek, jaw, and chin perimeter readable at thumbnail scale.
The upper and middle face read moderately longer than wide rather than compact-round.
The lateral cheek region is visibly wider than the jaw and anchors the contour on both sides.
The lower face narrows strongly and smoothly into a small softly rounded, slightly pointed chin.

The elongated upper-middle oval, cheek-owned width, strong continuous lower taper, and small chin are simultaneously visible without a label, surgery cue, isolated V, or styling effect substituting for them.

audit_boundary.explanation: Each face-shape pack contains strict visual_obligations but no moe_response or moe render_qualification object. The moe-specific auditor therefore reports schema failures; these are kept separate from the exact face-profile pixel gates above.

next_revision_hypothesis: For face-contour obligations, move bilateral temple and jaw clearance from a descriptive styling clause into a repeated high-priority capture invariant and explicitly reject loose side locks in the runtime negative prompt. Re-test on unrelated long-hair concepts before claiming render-fidelity promotion.
